title: Smarter ways to learn from failure
titleChinese: 从失败中学习的聪明方法
paragraphs: Many of us were told from an early age that, be it at school or in life, "you learn from your mistakes". But is this actually true?

The short answer is 'yes' – failure can be a teachable moment. But learning from our mistakes is, in reality, very hard because we don't like to fail. It doesn't feel good, so we react to failure in impulsive and emotional ways, like giving up on a task prematurely, telling ourselves we don't care whether we succeed, or finding fault with the task itself. This is self-protective, according to Hallgeir Sjåstad, a professor of psychology and leadership at the Norwegian School of Economics. "Most of us want to think of ourselves as competent and capable", he says, so when we fail "it poses a serious threat to our self-image".

Fortunately, there is research to suggest that there are some strategies to help us overcome the emotional barriers around failure. One of them is to adopt a third-person perspective. Instead of asking "Why did I fail?", we could ask "Why did Sam fail?", for example. Multiple studies by psychologist Ethan Kross at the University of Michigan show that adopting a third-person perspective helps to soften our negative emotional reactions, allowing us to look at failure more objectively.

A second strategy involves offering advice to others who may be in the same position as us. This strategy led to better levels of motivation and academic success in the test groups – involving both adults and children – that were asked to give advice based on their own failures. Professors Eskreis-Winkler, Fishbach and Duckworth found that the satisfaction of helping others "forces people to engage with their experience and what they have learned".

The writer Samuel Beckett once said: "fail again, fail better". But it now seems that we should be saying: "fail again, fail smarter". Failure is an inevitable part of life, but by learning to overcome the emotional barriers around it, we may find the road to success is a little easier to navigate.

vocabulary.entry: teachable moment /ˈtiːtʃəbl ˈməʊmənt/ 有教育意义的时刻；可从中学习的契机
vocabulary.example: Every difficult experience can be a teachable moment for personal growth.
vocabulary.translation: 每一次艰难的经历都能成为个人成长中一次可从中学习的契机。

vocabulary.entry: impulsive /ɪmˈpʌlsɪv/ adj. 冲动的；凭直觉行事的
vocabulary.example: She regretted her impulsive decision to quit the job without a plan.
vocabulary.translation: 她后悔自己一时冲动，没做任何计划就辞了职。

vocabulary.entry: prematurely /ˌpriːməˈtjʊəli/ adv. 过早地；仓促地
vocabulary.example: Don't judge the result prematurely before the project is completely finished.
vocabulary.translation: 在项目彻底完成前，不要过早地评判结果。

vocabulary.entry: find fault with /faɪnd fɔːlt wɪð/ 挑剔；找茬；对……吹毛求疵
vocabulary.example: He always finds fault with every detail instead of giving practical suggestions.
vocabulary.translation: 他总对每个细节吹毛求疵，却从不出具实际的建议。

vocabulary.entry: self-protective /ˌself prəˈtektɪv/ adj. 自我保护的
vocabulary.example: Her quiet attitude is a self-protective response to the hurt she suffered before.
vocabulary.translation: 她沉默的态度是对过往所受伤害的一种自我保护反应。

vocabulary.entry: psychology /saɪˈkɒlədʒi/ n. 心理学；心理状态
vocabulary.example: He studied psychology at university and now works as a professional counselor.
vocabulary.translation: 他大学主修心理学，如今是一名专业的心理咨询师。

vocabulary.entry: leadership /ˈliːdəʃɪp/ n. 领导力；领导才能
vocabulary.example: The company is looking for a manager with strong leadership and communication skills.
vocabulary.translation: 公司正在寻找一位兼具出色领导力和沟通能力的经理。

vocabulary.entry: competent /ˈkɒmpɪtənt/ adj. 有能力的；能胜任的；称职的
vocabulary.example: She is a competent teacher who can connect with students of all ages.
vocabulary.translation: 她是一位称职的老师，能和各个年龄段的学生建立良好沟通。

vocabulary.entry: capable /ˈkeɪpəbl/ adj. 有才能的；能干的；有能力做的
vocabulary.example: Anyone who is willing to learn is capable of mastering this basic skill.
vocabulary.translation: 任何愿意学习的人，都能掌握这项基础技能。

vocabulary.entry: pose /pəʊz/ v. 造成；带来（威胁、问题等）
vocabulary.example: This new policy could pose a potential threat to the development of small businesses.
vocabulary.translation: 这项新政策可能会给小企业的发展带来潜在威胁。

vocabulary.entry: self-image /ˌself ˈɪmɪdʒ/ n. 自我形象；自我认知
vocabulary.example: Constant criticism from others can easily damage a person's self-image.
vocabulary.translation: 他人的不断指责很容易损害一个人的自我形象。

vocabulary.entry: strategy /ˈstrætədʒi/ n. 策略；行动计划；方法
vocabulary.example: We need to develop a new marketing strategy to attract more young customers.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要制定新的营销策略，来吸引更多年轻消费者。

vocabulary.entry: overcome /ˌəʊvəˈkʌm/ v. 克服；战胜；攻克
vocabulary.example: She managed to overcome her fear of public speaking after months of practice.
vocabulary.translation: 经过数月的练习，她成功克服了对公开演讲的恐惧。

vocabulary.entry: emotional barrier /ɪˈməʊʃənl ˈbæriə(r)/ 情感障碍；情绪阻碍
vocabulary.example: Lack of trust has become the main emotional barrier between the two sides.
vocabulary.translation: 缺乏信任已经成为双方之间主要的情感障碍。

vocabulary.entry: adopt /əˈdɒpt/ v. 采用；采取；运用
vocabulary.example: The school decided to adopt a new teaching method to improve learning efficiency.
vocabulary.translation: 这所学校决定采用一种新的教学方法，来提升学习效率。

vocabulary.entry: third-person perspective /ˌθɜːd ˈpɜːsn pəˈspektɪv/ 第三人称视角
vocabulary.example: Looking at the problem from a third-person perspective helps you see the whole picture.
vocabulary.translation: 从第三人称视角看待问题，能帮你看清事情的全貌。

vocabulary.entry: soften /ˈsɒfn/ v. 缓和；减轻；使温和
vocabulary.example: A sincere apology can soften his anger and make communication possible again.
vocabulary.translation: 一句真诚的道歉能缓和他的怒气，让沟通重新成为可能。

vocabulary.entry: negative emotional reaction /ˈneɡətɪv ɪˈməʊʃənl riˈækʃn/ 负面情绪反应
vocabulary.example: Yelling and crying are common negative emotional reactions to frustration.
vocabulary.translation: 大喊和哭泣是面对挫败感时常见的负面情绪反应。

vocabulary.entry: objectively /əbˈdʒektɪvli/ adv. 客观地；不带偏见地
vocabulary.example: We need to analyze the data objectively instead of making subjective judgments.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要客观地分析数据，而非做出主观的判断。

vocabulary.entry: academic success /ˌækəˈdemɪk səkˈses/ 学业成功；学术成就
vocabulary.example: Hard work and effective learning methods are the keys to academic success.
vocabulary.translation: 努力付出和有效的学习方法，是学业成功的关键。

vocabulary.entry: test group /ˈtest ɡruːp/ 试验组；测试组
vocabulary.example: The test group showed significant improvement after using the new training method.
vocabulary.translation: 试验组在采用新的训练方法后，表现出了显著的进步。

vocabulary.entry: satisfaction /ˌsætɪsˈfækʃn/ n. 满足感；成就感；满意
vocabulary.example: She felt a great sense of satisfaction after finishing the challenging project.
vocabulary.translation: 完成这个具有挑战性的项目后，她感受到了强烈的成就感。

vocabulary.entry: engage with /ɪnˈɡeɪdʒ wɪð/ 深入思考；认真对待；参与
vocabulary.example: It's important to engage with your work if you want to achieve meaningful results.
vocabulary.translation: 如果你想取得有价值的成果，认真对待工作至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: inevitable /ɪnˈevɪtəbl/ adj. 不可避免的；必然发生的
vocabulary.example: Change is an inevitable part of life and we have to learn to adapt to it.
vocabulary.translation: 变化是生活中不可避免的一部分，我们必须学会去适应。

vocabulary.entry: navigate /ˈnævɪɡeɪt/ v. 顺利应对；处理；驾驭
vocabulary.example: She has the ability to navigate complex social situations with confidence and ease.
vocabulary.translation: 她有能力自信且从容地应对复杂的社交场合。

sentences.chinese: 比如，不要问“我为什么失败了？”，而是问“山姆为什么失败了？”。

sentences.english: Multiple studies by psychologist Ethan Kross at the University of Michigan show that adopting a third-person perspective helps to soften our negative emotional reactions, allowing us to look at failure more objectively.

sentences.english: The writer Samuel Beckett once said: "fail again, fail better".
sentences.chinese: 作家塞缪尔·贝克特曾说过：“再试一次，败得更漂亮些。”

sentences.chinese: 但现在我们似乎应该说：“再试一次，败得更明智些。”
